meta.title: Paul Becomes a Believer | Ananias Helps Paul
meta.verseText: Let us not become tired of doing good. At the right time we will gather a crop if we don't give up.
meta.theme: God can help you see things in a new way.

questions.text: What was the name of the man who was traveling to Damascus to arrest Jesus-followers?
questions.hint: He was later known as Paul.
questions.explanation: Saul was a Jewish religious leader who got permission to travel to Damascus to arrest people who loved and followed Jesus.

questions.text: What other name was Saul known by?
questions.hint: It starts with the same letter as 'pray.'
questions.explanation: Saul was also sometimes known as Paul. After he became a Jesus-follower, he became famous as the apostle Paul.

questions.text: What city was Saul traveling to when he met Jesus?
questions.hint: It starts with a D.
questions.explanation: Saul was on the road to Damascus to arrest Jesus-followers there when Jesus stopped him.

questions.text: What happened to Saul after he met Jesus on the road?
questions.hint: It had to do with his eyes.
questions.explanation: After meeting Jesus on the road, Saul became blind and had to be led into the city of Damascus.

questions.text: Who did God send to pray for Saul so he could see again?
questions.hint: His name starts with an A.
questions.explanation: God spoke to a man named Ananias, who went to Saul, prayed for him, and Saul could see again.

questions.text: True or False: Before meeting Jesus, Saul was kind to Jesus-followers.
questions.explanation: Saul was NOT kind to Jesus-followers. He believed their teaching was dangerous and tried to arrest them.

questions.text: True or False: Saul learned to see Jesus in a totally new way.
questions.explanation: Yes! Saul once thought Jesus' teachings were dangerous lies, but after meeting Jesus, he became one of His most loyal followers.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: God can help you see things in a ___ way.
questions.hint: It's our Bottom Line for today!
questions.explanation: The Bottom Line for this lesson is, 'God can help you see things in a new way.'

questions.text: Which book of the Bible tells the story of Saul meeting Jesus?
questions.hint: It's a book about what the disciples did after Jesus rose.
questions.explanation: The story of Saul becoming Paul is found in Acts chapter 9.

questions.text: Who appeared and spoke to Saul on the road to Damascus?
questions.hint: It was the same person Saul was fighting against.
questions.explanation: Jesus Himself appeared and spoke to Saul on the road, changing his life forever.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: Saul thought Jesus' teachings were ___ lies.
questions.explanation: Before meeting Jesus, Saul believed the teachings about Jesus were so dangerous that he wanted to stop them.

questions.text: What did Saul start doing after he became a Jesus-follower?
questions.hint: He told everyone about Jesus.
questions.explanation: After Saul became a Jesus-follower, he started preaching about Jesus everywhere he went.

questions.text: Why did Saul have to escape from Damascus and Jerusalem?
options: The religious leaders didn't like him preaching about Jesus
He wanted to go on vacation
questions.hint: The same people Saul used to work with were now upset with him.
questions.explanation: The religious leaders didn't like that Saul was now telling people about Jesus, so he had to escape from both cities.

questions.text: True or False: God can help us see other people in a new way too.
questions.explanation: Yes! We can ask the Holy Spirit to help us see the people in our lives the way God sees them.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: Let us not become tired of doing ___.
questions.hint: From our memory verse, Galatians 6:9.
questions.explanation: Our memory verse says, 'Let us not become tired of doing good.'

questions.text: According to Galatians 6:9, what will happen if we don't give up doing good?
questions.hint: Think about a farmer at harvest time.
questions.explanation: The verse promises that at the right time, we will gather a crop if we don't give up — God promises something good!

questions.text: What does 'gather a crop' mean in our memory verse?
options: We will receive something good from God
questions.hint: A crop is the good result of hard work.
questions.explanation: Crops are good things — food that grows because of hard work. The verse promises God will give us something good if we keep doing good.

questions.text: Who lives inside every Jesus-follower to help them?
questions.hint: It's the third person of the Trinity.
questions.explanation: After Jesus went back to heaven, His Holy Spirit came to live inside every Jesus-follower to help them.

questions.text: Why was Ananias probably afraid to go pray for Saul?
options: It was too far to walk
questions.hint: Think about Saul's reputation.
questions.explanation: Ananias only saw Saul as a threat because Saul had been arresting Jesus-followers, but Jesus helped Ananias see that Saul could change.

questions.text: What is the point of your life, according to today's lesson?
options: To show and tell people about Jesus
questions.hint: Paul learned this when he met Jesus.
questions.explanation: The lesson teaches that the point of your life is to show and tell people about the love of Jesus.

questions.text: How can you live like Jesus?
options: By being kind, trustworthy, and full of joy
questions.hint: Think of His character.
questions.explanation: We live like Jesus when we're kind, trustworthy, and filled with joy like He is.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: You can tell people about Jesus by explaining why you ___ the way you do.
questions.explanation: You can tell people about Jesus by explaining why you live the way you do — because you're being like Him!

questions.text: If a kid at school says mean stuff, what might really be going on?
options: They could be lonely or hurting
questions.hint: Try to see them the way God sees them.
questions.explanation: Maybe that rude kid is just lonely, and no one is kind to them at home. God can help us see people in a new way.

questions.text: What can you do when your little brother or sister seems annoying?
options: Ask God to help you see them the way He does
questions.explanation: Maybe they actually think you're amazing and just want to be with you! Ask the Holy Spirit to show you how God sees them.

questions.text: True or False: Saul gave up on God's plan after meeting Jesus.
questions.explanation: False! Saul (Paul) didn't give up. Even when religious leaders tried to stop him, he kept preaching about Jesus.

questions.text: What did Saul learn the real point of his life was?
options: To be the most powerful leader
questions.hint: It changed after he met Jesus.
questions.explanation: Paul learned that the point of his life was to tell people about Jesus — not just to follow rules.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: God wants us to know He has a wonderful ___ for our lives.
questions.explanation: Even when things happen that we don't understand, we can trust God's wonderful plan for our lives.

questions.text: What did Saul pride himself on before meeting Jesus?
options: Following every single one of God's laws
questions.hint: He was a religious leader.
questions.explanation: Saul was a Jewish religious leader who had studied under a famous teacher, and he prided himself on following every single one of God's laws.

questions.text: True or False: Only adults can tell others about Jesus.
questions.explanation: False! Kids can tell people about Jesus too — by being kind, trustworthy, and joyful, and by explaining why they live the way they do.

questions.text: Why is it good to ask the Holy Spirit to help us see people?
options: So we can see them the way God sees them
So we can become smarter than them
So we can win against them
questions.hint: God sees the whole heart of every person.
questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit helps us see people the way God sees them — with love and compassion, not just on the surface.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: At the right time we will gather a crop if we don't ___ up.
questions.hint: It's part of our memory verse.
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:9 says, 'At the right time we will gather a crop if we don't give up.'

questions.text: What did Jesus' followers do after He went back to heaven?
options: They told people everywhere about God's love
questions.explanation: After Jesus went to heaven, His followers, filled with the Holy Spirit, told people everywhere about God and His great love!

questions.text: What should we do when doing the right thing feels hard?
options: Keep going and trust God's promise
questions.hint: Remember Galatians 6:9.
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:9 reminds us not to become tired of doing good. If we don't give up, God promises we'll gather something good.

story.summary: Saul was a Jewish religious leader who thought he had it all together. He believed the teachings about Jesus were dangerous lies and got permission to travel to Damascus to arrest Jesus-followers there. But on the road, Saul met Jesus and became blind. God sent a man named Ananias to pray for Saul, and Saul could see again — both with his eyes and with his heart! Saul became a Jesus-follower and started preaching about Jesus everywhere. The religious leaders didn't like that, so he had to escape from Damascus and then from Jerusalem. But because Saul learned to see Jesus in a totally new way, many, many more people learned about Him. God can help us see things in a new way too.

scenes.title: Saul the Persecutor
scenes.description: Saul was a Jewish religious leader who studied under a famous teacher. He prided himself on following every one of God's laws. He believed the stories about Jesus were dangerous lies, and he was not kind to people who loved and followed Jesus. He got permission to travel to other places to arrest Jesus-followers.

scenes.title: Road to Damascus
scenes.description: On his way to Damascus to arrest more Jesus-followers, Saul suddenly met Jesus on the road. Jesus spoke to him, and Saul became blind. The men with him had to lead him by the hand into the city.

scenes.title: Ananias Prays for Saul
scenes.description: While Saul was blind in Damascus, God spoke to a Jesus-follower named Ananias. Ananias was probably scared because Saul had been hurting Jesus-followers — but he obeyed God. He went to Saul, prayed for him, and Saul could see again. Saul became a Jesus-follower!

scenes.title: From Saul to Paul, Preaching Everywhere
scenes.description: Saul, now also called Paul, started preaching about Jesus right away. The religious leaders didn't like this and tried to stop him, so he had to escape from Damascus and later from Jerusalem too. But because Saul learned to see Jesus in a new way, many, many more people learned about Him.

scenes.title: Seeing in a New Way
scenes.description: God can help us see our lives, the people around us, and the world in a new way. The Holy Spirit helps us see people the way God sees them — even a sibling that seems annoying or a kid at school who is unkind. And Galatians 6:9 reminds us not to give up on doing good.
